title: Control plane: add key-version pinning + validation for KMS KEK refs
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: - Adds explicit key version pinning for GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault KEKs; disallows unpinned key refs by default for new installs. - Disallows AWS KMS aliases as KEKs (must use Key ARN/Key ID) to avoid accidental drift. - Provides migration path for existing tenants via a reconcile-time pinning step + temporary compatibility flag.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces deterministic KMS key selection in the encryption config schema by requiring version-pinned KEK references (where the provider supports versions) and by rejecting ambiguous/unsafe key references that can silently drift during rollouts (e.g. AWS aliases, GCP CryptoKey without CryptoKeyVersion, Azure key identifier without version). This is the first slice of ENG-4221 and supports the KMS rotation hardening workstream (ENG-4217).

Motivation: We have multiple reports (and one staging canary incident during failure-mode testing) where encryption config changes + controller reconciliation caused subtle differences in which key material was used for new encrypt operations. When the key reference is not version-pinned, a later rotation (or alias retarget) can cause a mixed-state where encrypt uses one key while decrypt paths assume another, and/or different clusters pick different targets during a rollout.

Design: 1) Schema change: Introduce explicit fields to represent a pinned KEK reference: - provider=aws: require Key ARN/Key ID (reject alias/* for KEKs) - provider=gcp: require cryptoKeyVersion (projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*/cryptoKeyVersions/*) - provider=azure: require versioned key identifier (https://{vault}.vault.azure.net/keys/{name}/{version}) 2) Validation: On config apply/update we validate that the KEK reference is pinned and matches the provider-specific format. Unsafe configs fail closed with actionable errors (and remediation suggestions). 3) Migration logic: For existing tenants (especially Private), we need backward compatibility and staged rollout: - Existing configs that are unpinned are accepted only when the feature flag encryption.kms.allow_unpinned_kek_refs=true is enabled (default: true for existing installs, false for new installs). - During reconcile, if the flag is enabled and the provider supports versions (GCP/Azure), the controller resolves the current active/latest enabled version deterministically and writes the pinned version back into the persisted config state ("pin-on-reconcile"). - For AWS, we cannot pin backing key material versions in the KMS API; instead we ensure the reference is non-aliased (Key ID/ARN). Existing alias-based refs will be surfaced as warnings with a deprecation deadline and a one-click suggested replacement in Console (separate follow-up).

User-visible behavior: - New installs (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with unpinned GCP/Azure key refs will see a 400 with an explicit validation error at config apply time. - Existing installs will continue to work during the migration window; once the controller pins the version, subsequent deploys/rollouts will remain stable. - AWS: attempts to set alias/* will fail with: "AWS KMS KEK reference must be a Key ARN or Key ID; aliases are not allowed for KEKs".

Key implementation details: - Added KmsKekRefV2 to the control-plane encryption config model with provider-specific parsing + normalization. - Implemented ParseAndNormalizeKekRef(provider, ref) returning a canonical string used for equality checks and audit logging. - Added controller reconcile step to pin versions for gcp/azure when allow_unpinned_kek_refs is enabled. - Added structured validation errors with remediation pointers (docs links are placeholders until ENG-4246 lands). - Added metrics for migration/pinning outcomes: encryption_kms_kek_pin_attempt_total{provider,outcome} and encryption_kms_kek_validation_failure_total{provider,reason}.

Files / areas changed (high level): - controlplane/encryption/config/schema.go: schema types + serialization changes - controlplane/encryption/config/validate.go: provider-specific validation and error strings - controlplane/encryption/kms/refs/*.go: parsing + normalization helpers for aws/gcp/azure - controlplane/controllers/tenant_encryption_controller.go: pin-on-reconcile migration logic + feature flag gate - console/api/encryption_config.ts: surfaced validation errors (no UI changes beyond error display) - docs/internal/ops/encryption-config-migration.md: migration notes for on-call + Private operators - tests: unit tests for parsing/validation; integration test for reconcile pinning behavior

Illustrative snippet (GCP validation error): Input: projects/p/locations/us/keyRings/r/cryptoKeys/kek Output error: "GCP KMS KEK reference must include cryptoKeyVersion. Example: projects/.../cryptoKeys/kek/cryptoKeyVersions/5"

Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (this PR): land schema + validation behind flags; default allow_unpinned_kek_refs=true for existing tenants. - Stage 2 (ENG-4242 / Private): installer preflight will warn/fail if unpinned refs are detected depending on install vs upgrade. - Stage 3: flip default allow_unpinned_kek_refs=false for all new tenants; then progressively for existing after we confirm >99% have been auto-pinned.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for parsing/validation - [x] Integration test for reconcile pinning path - [x] Feature flag added + documented (defaulted for backwards compatibility) - [x] Added metrics + wired to existing control-plane metrics registry - [x] Manual test in staging with GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault - [ ] Follow-up: docs public-facing wording and screenshots (ENG-4246)

Notes for reviewers: The main risk is accidental lockout if we validate too aggressively. I tried to keep the migration path safe: existing tenants are not blocked unless they toggle the flag off. The reconcile pinning step writes back only if it can resolve a single enabled version; if it finds multiple enabled versions and cannot choose deterministically, it will refuse to pin and emit an actionable event.

Review conversation (highlights): Marcus Lin: "We should fail closed for new installs, but we cannot risk bricking existing tenants. The flag defaulting behavior looks good. Please ensure the error messages don’t leak full customer resource IDs into shared logs." Benji Okafor (author): "Updated: validation errors are returned to the caller, but server logs now include only a hashed ref + provider; full ref is kept in the tenant-scoped audit event only." Jordan Lee: "What is the deterministic selection rule for GCP if the user provides only a CryptoKey?" Benji: "We don’t auto-select on apply. We only auto-pin during reconcile when allow_unpinned_kek_refs is true, and we pick the latest enabled version by integer version ID. If multiple enabled versions exist and the latest is disabled/unknown, we fail pinning with a warning and require operator action." Hanae Suzuki: "For Private, we need a clear operator runbook step: confirm IAM perms to list versions (GCP) / get versions (Azure)." Benji: "Added to internal migration notes; installer preflight improvements are coming in ENG-4242." Ethan Park: "LGTM; please add a metric for validation failures by reason for alert tuning." Benji: "Added encryption_kms_kek_validation_failure_total with reason label." 

CI: - build-and-test (pass) - lint (pass) - controlplane-integration (pass) - console-typecheck (pass)

Merge: Squash merged into main.
commits: validation: fail unsafe/unpinned KEK refs with actionable errors
controller: add pin-on-reconcile migration step behind allow_unpinned_kek_refs
metrics: export pin attempts + validation failures counters
tests: unit + integration coverage for pinning and error paths
docs/internal: add migration notes for operators and on-call
changed_areas: Control plane encryption config schema + validation
Console API error propagation (no UI overhaul)
